# `hs-run setup` — state map

<!-- generated by render_state_map.py — edit the SSOT, # learn: "${HARNESS_BIN_ROOT:-.}"/harness/data/hs-run-registry.d/<domain>.yaml, not this file -->

Every state `hs-run setup` can report, with what it means. Run the CLI, read the `state`, do the judgment that state names, run it again — each state is re-derived from artifacts on disk, so deleting an artifact regresses the state.

This file is generated. Change the source named in the comment above, then re-render with `render_state_map.py`; edits made here are lost on the next render.

## States that route something

The CLI hands these rule and reference paths over at the moment the step begins — the body does not repeat them.

| state | what it means | routes |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_legacy` | The live terminal-voice file still carries a pre-split key. Clear it with a voice_prefs re-save before any group is walked. | `references/schema-migration.md` |
| `trust_needed` | This repo is not in the trust store, so a standards rule's shell detector stays grep-only. Ask before granting; never grant silently. | `references/trust-repo.md` |

## States that route nothing

Not a gap: each is fully served by the `next_action` line the envelope already carries, and needs no extra file to act on.

| state | what it means |
|---|---|
| `policy_unreadable` | A configuration source could not be read at all. The envelope's warnings carry the underlying error; repair it before configuring anything. |
| `deps_missing` | A required package is absent. Later hooks and tests fail with opaque ImportErrors until it is installed; nothing else here is worth reading yet. |
| `configured` | Deps present, no legacy keys, repo trusted. Every remaining choice belongs to the user — ask rather than assume a default. |
